reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: § 6(a) gives Contractor a convenience right on only 15 days' notice, squarely inside the rule's walk-away zone (<90 days), and conditions our own convenience exit on there being no open Statement of Work, which in a task-by-task SOW structure under an evergreen term leaves us without a practical exit.

The redline reaches the preferred position with the necessary rewrite: a Company 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, with refund of prepaid fees and express exclusion of penalty/early-termination charge/acceleration, and Contractor's convenience right pushed to 90 days' notice and only when no SOW is open — consistent with the model language.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check is a phrasing artifact: the operative party name in this contract is 'Company', an accepted Customer alias, and the clause plainly grants us the convenience right.

The 0.737 changed-character ratio is justified — the original clause is a single symmetric sentence that must be split to add our right and lengthen Contractor's notice; no smaller edit achieves both.
